Fixes: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/4866
Here's the first implementation: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4986

To summarize, in the first solution we're trying to find if there's an identical route for the current one being added only with the `HEAD` method by comparing `url`, `path`, and `constraints`.
This approach works for most cases, but we can't compare two paths `/:param1` with `/:param2`.
Comparing them will give `false`, even though it's the same path. 
Still, this works, mainly because the previous implementation with the `router.find` function gave a lot of "false positives", which led to missing routes since we're not adding them. With the first solution, the comparison is stricter, so even if we compare two routes, like `/:param1` and `/:param2` and we get `false`, the worst thing that can happen is that `router.on` will fail, and the user will have to figure out that he needs to define the routes in a different way since there are duplications.

If we want to give a 100% solution we should go for one of the following implementations:
1. Parse the `opts.url`, and then compare it to the `pattern` field in the `router.routes` object.
for example, the pattern will be `/:` but the current route will be `/:param2` - which needs to be parsed to `/:`.
2. Use the `router.on` method for validation, as I did here. This way the app behaves exactly how it is supposed to.
As said here: https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/issues/332 Implementing the `has` function to `find-my-way` needs to use part of the `router.on` method. Meaning, that using the `router.on` method can give us an accurate result to understand if a route exists in the router. So, as long as `has` does not exist, I think using that will be the best way to go.

Luckily, I tried this other implementation, since I found other bugs while implementing.
1. `router.off` method should get `constraints`, and not `{ constraints }`. 
Also, the `url`, is supposed to be not the current one - `opts.url`, it needs to be the one **found** in the router already. If it's not the same, it won't be deleted from the `router`.
So it should be `router.off('HEAD', headHandler.store.config.url, constraints)` instead of `router.off('HEAD', opts.url, { constraints })`

2. Also, take a look at the `isDuplication` variable. The message returned by `router.on` method in case of duplication ends with `/:`, which is `pattern`, and `opts.url` is actually `/:param2`. Therefore, `isDuplication` will always be false.

(Didn't know if I should open different bugs on those two, so I just fixed them as part of the implementation because I thought it was necessary)

Let me know what you guys think about this option.

issue_context.title: HEAD requests are resolving to wildcard routes instead of named routes
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported


### Fastify version

4.0.0

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

20.3.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

macOS Ventura 13.4.1

### Description

A HEAD request to a named route is resolving to the wildcard route instead while GET requests resolve correctly.

### Steps to Reproduce

I've put a simple repo here https://github.com/andokai/head-issue

The issue is demonstrated in the failing test in `example.test.js`.

### Expected Behavior

The content-length header for the HEAD request should match the equivalent header for the GET request and it shouldn't match the header for the GET request of the wildcard route.
comments:
Hello @andokai,

I have just tested a snippet to handle both `GET` and `HEAD` requests, and they are functioning correctly in my case. It's worth mentioning that we don't need to explicitly set up a separate route for `HEAD` requests since they automatically go through the `GET` route. I used Postman to verify the `content-length` attribute, and it consistently showed the same value of 909 in both cases. You can find the snippet of the headers I received for both requests in the following image:

![image](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/assets/50861363/82e56f19-8a16-4604-8d77-c15d87697b3e)

Additionally, here is the link to my gist for reference: [https://gist.github.com/ashutoshdhande/4895b5ae808ed985c0c821a375425153](url)

If any update please provide.

I'm running into constant OOM issues when trying to benchmark the solution. I imagine is because of the doubled number of routes and checks.

I'm imagining that we can do several optimizations here.

The whole check to the `HEAD` routes is duplicated, I think we can do it within this [line](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/5009/files#diff-cf6996cafd1df0bc168a5c5f3a7470f11fc3aea9f908091d5dd6be2e7b30a2c3R413) so we remove duplicated logic. What we're doing in the `main` branch is: checking if a route exists using find > if so, under certain circumstances, remove if > set `headHandler` and `hasHEADHandler` accordingly to the rest of the code, and use them.

So, I kept it as it is, in the same location.
Also, I didn't add this check, this check exists already. The only thing that was doubled is the `router.on` `router.off` operations, which are instead of calling `router.find`.
